messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created (INC-1973509876) - Multiple CUDA OOMs observed on prod-serving-pool-07 affecting model variants in us-west-2. Auto-alert from node-monitor.

alex: seeing repeated OOMs on node prod-srv-07b even though headroom reports ~2GB free on GPU0. Containers getting killed mid-inference. Node is flapping containers.

sana: confirmed. stacktrace shows allocator failing to reserve contiguous blocks. weirdly headroom metric from headroom-exporter is still positive. pasted relevant logs below.

sana: ```
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] allocator: reserve_claim id=0x7fa3 size=524288000 -> fail: no contiguous block
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] kvcache: pinned 120MB, available_headroom=2048MB
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] cuda-driver: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (error 2)
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] containerd: kill -9 pid=4321 (oom)
```

mike: two hypotheses: (1) fragmentation + reserved-blocks = inability to service a large contiguous allocation, (2) headroom metric is reporting logical free bytes but doesn't account for reserved/sparepool pinned fragmentation. we've seen something similar with KV-cache reservation patterns.

jen: customer impact - increase in 5xxs and tail latency for the streaming route of model "redwood-alpha-1". Pager shows ~12% failed requests across a subset of pods. Not all pods on the node are affected.

oncall-pager: Paging/Alerting: customer-impact=true, Sev2. CC: infra-oncall. Notifying customers via status page (partial degradation).

alex: quick mitigations I want to try now: (A) evict KV cache on affected containers to free pinned pages, (B) reduce batch sizes on live route via runtime config, (C) restart worst-offending container to drop fragmented allocations. will coordinate one at a time.

opsbot: running eviction command on pod serving-rapi-77 (prod-srv-07b):
```bash
kubectl exec -n prod pod/serving-rapi-77 -- /opt/runtime/bin/evict-kvcache --force --target=all
```

opsbot: evict command returned: evicted 128MB pinned KV entries, KV cache size now 64MB.

alex: re-run repro after eviction: still hitting cudaMalloc OOM on next large batch request (alloc ~480MB). nvidia-smi snapshot:
```
GPU 0: 16179MiB / 24576MiB used
Processes: 25 running, top consumer runtime-worker(4321) 7400MiB, sparepool reserved 4096MiB, kvcache pinned 64MiB
```

mike: note sparepool/reserved blocks show up as "reserved 4096MiB" - if the allocator needs a single contiguous 480MB chunk but free space is fragmented into many small holes due to previously reserved blocks it will fail even though sum(free) > 480MB. we've hit a reserve accounting race where released reservations aren't merged back fast enough.

jen: quick customer mitigation: route traffic for that model away from nodes with sparepool reservations until we have a root cause. can we update routing policy?

alex: initiating temporary routing rule - scale up healthy pool and mark prod-serving-pool-07 as avoid via routing tag. command: `apictl routing update --tag avoid:prod-serving-pool-07 --model redwood-alpha-1`

opsbot: routing update applied. traffic diverted (approx 65% of affected requests now rerouted). visible drop in failures for rerouted requests.

sana: root-cause hypothesis: allocator's reserve-merge path occasionally fails under concurrency leading to fragmentation and ghost reserved blocks. There's a race where reserve-release doesn't coalesce with adjacent free blocks until GC runs, and simultaneous new reservations can fragment the heap such that large contiguous allocations fail. We need a reproducible test and a short-term mitigation in runtime.

mike: immediate runtime-change candidate: allow kernel to fall back to slower CPU-backed allocation for the final fallback path (spill-to-host) for large single allocations so we don't OOM, but that increases latency. For now prefer routing and evicting caches instead of falling back globally.

alex: performed a targeted container restart for pod serving-rapi-77 (killed only runtime-worker PID 4321). container came back up and service on that pod restored. post-restart: `nvidia-smi` shows fragmentation cleared and the next allocation succeeded.

jen: good. still seeing a couple of nodes with repeat failures (prod-srv-07a and 07b). I'll open a task to purge sparepool reservations and add a guard in the autoscaler to prefer nodes with contiguous free blocks (short-term heuristic).

sana: taking lead for the postmortem and next-steps. action items I have right now: (1) reproduce locally with fragmentation harness, (2) add metrics for contiguous-free-chunks and avg-largest-chunk-size, (3) patch allocator to coalesce on release path, (4) add runtime flag to enable spill-to-host for large allocations as a controlled opt-in.

alex: handoff to sana for next 4 hours while I monitor routing/traffic. I'm leaving this thread pinned to incidents.

oncall-pager: Handoff acknowledged. sana is the new on-call investigator.

incident-bot: Status update: mitigated -> partial (traffic rerouted, targeted restarts). Impact: degraded performance for customers on redwood-alpha-1 during mitigation window. Severity: SEV2. Postmortem required.

jen: creating postmortem doc and linking logs/heap-dumps in the ticket. will tag eng-runtime and eng-ml for model-level risk assessment.

sana: noted. I'll capture the experiment and add the reproducer. Also scheduling replay with allocator team tomorrow.

alex: thanks all. follow-ups: limit production large contiguous allocations while we fix allocator, improve headroom metric to account for fragmentation/reserved blocks, and get an automated eviction command for high-risk pods.

incident-bot: Incident INC-1973509876 closed for on-call activity, follow-ups tracked in PM-19735.
